fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes enter the fuzz harness; length is capped at 32767 and copied into the static global data_copy[32767].
memmem finds the 4-byte sequence \r\n\r\n somewhere in the input; because it is not at offset 0, FINALIZER_DONE is returned and parsing proceeds.
STRING_SWITCH reads 4 bytes from the start of the buffer; input does not begin with PROXY or \r\n\r\n, so buffer is returned unchanged.
Leading whitespace is skipped; the request begins with a valid HTTP method so buffer is unchanged.
Reads 4 bytes from buffer; matches GET/POST/HEAD etc. and returns a pointer just past the method token.
Finds the first \r in the request line; the byte after it is treated as the start of the header section even if it is not \n.
Returns a pointer to the byte after the \r; parse_headers is then called with this pointer.

fine_trace.code: for (p = buffer + 1; n_headers < N_HEADER_START && buffer_end > p;)
fine_trace.note: Header scan starts one byte past the request-line terminator; each header line is recorded as (start,end) pairs in header_start[].
A short header such as 'Cont' near the end of the buffer is recorded; its end pointer points to the \r that terminates the header line.
Reads 4 bytes from the header start; for a header 'Cont' placed at offset length-8, the 4 bytes are within the buffer and match the 'Cont' case.
p is advanced by 7 (sizeof("Content")-1) past the end of the header name; the subsequent STRING_SWITCH_L reads 4 bytes from this advanced pointer.
The 4-byte read from the advanced p crosses the end of the 32767-byte global data_copy array, causing a global-buffer-overflow READ 1.
